model.rationale: The post-redistricting fundamentals give Democrats a roughly 25-point lean, and the resource gap is lopsided in Haynes's favor, with markets pricing this as a near-certain Democratic hold. Nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending on Jackson's side would be the first sign the margin could narrow.

overview:
TX-30 is an open seat in a Dallas-area district drawn to be solidly Democratic, with a partisan lean of about 25 points. Frederick Haynes III, the Democratic nominee, has raised over $420,000 and holds about $120,000 on hand, supplemented by roughly $200,000 in outside support. Republican Everett Jackson has raised about $17,000 with minimal cash remaining.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the stark financial imbalance. Prediction markets price the Democratic candidate around 95% to win. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the expected margin in the mid-20s.
